subject: Dedicated GPU pool: throughput SLO math, p99 latency floor, and billing bands
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>, Peter Chen <p.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool: throughput SLO math, p99 latency floor, and billing bands

Hi Sarah / Peter,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, we put together a concise pricing + SLA framing for a Dedicated GPU pool that meets Acme's throughput and latency needs while keeping reserved commit economics simple. High level summary below; attached is a draft pricing model and the benchmark runner we plan to use.

Key guarantees (proposal):
- Committed throughput band (tokens/sec): 100k / 250k / 500k
- Measured SLA: commit is verified via steady-state throughput at the model & prompt mix below, sustained for 30 minutes.
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms (single-token generation latency at steady-state, 16-token prompt priming as measurement).
- Burst behavior: system permits short bursts (+20%) for up to 2 minutes; bursts not counted toward committed baseline.
- Billing: per-band reserved monthly fee + overage priced per 10k tokens/sec-hour. Example bands in attached spreadsheet.
- Commit term: 12 months minimum; pricing tiers improve at 12/24/36 month commits.

Measurement methodology (short):
- Model used for verification: Redwood-34B-quant (customer-visible variant).
- Tokenization: BPE; include detokenization pass to count real token output.
- Prompt length distribution: 60% short (<=32 tokens), 30% mid (33-128), 10% long (129-512). We will run separate bucketed runs and combine weighted results.
- Warm-up: 10 minute warm-up, then 30 minute steady-state measurement window.
- KV cache: included in baseline (i.e., standard chat sessions will leverage cache); we will also run an uncached pass for absolute worst-case latency.

Open items for your input: exact prompt mix (we used a representative sample), any regulatory constraints on measurement endpoints (IP allowlist), and whether Acme needs explicit fallback credit if we route to a lower capacity pool.

Attachments: draft_pricing_model.xlsx, acme_benchmark_script_v1.py

Looking forward to your feedback — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through numbers.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft_pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: acme_benchmark_script_v1.py (script)]
From: Peter Chen <p.chen@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool: throughput SLO math, p99 latency floor, and billing bands

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we share internally with ops/procurement: 

1) Measurement specifics: what model weights and quantization are you using for the verification run? Do we get the exact binary?
2) Sequence length mix: can you provide the exact sample set you used to weight short/mid/long? Our production has more mid/long than you listed.
3) Burst vs committed: if we hit sustained bursts beyond 2 minutes during peak, how do overages get counted? Is there a smoothing window?
4) Fallback credit: if Redwood routes to a lower-tier model or different region during an incident, will Acme get credit toward monthly usage or a service credit?

Also, one procurement note: if the billing bands are tied to tokens/sec, how do you map from requests/sec for our routing and autoscaling rules? We typically size by RPS.

Can you add a short appendix answering these points and resend?

—Peter
Director of Infrastructure, Acme Analytics
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chen <p.chen@acme-analytics.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-14T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool: throughput SLO math, p99 latency floor, and billing bands

Peter — appreciate the rapid questions, nice ones. Answers below and I embedded the explicit sample mix in the attached CSV.

1) Model: verification runs use Redwood-34B-quant (8-bit Q4 variant used in GPU pools). We supply the inference container + hash-verified model artifact for the verification window; customers do not receive raw bits outside the container.

2) Sample set: attached benchmark_results_v1.csv includes the per-run counts. For Acme I propose shifting weights to 45% short / 40% mid / 15% long given your note — that will slightly reduce tokens/sec on the same RPS but aligns closer to your telemetry.

3) Burst accounting: overages are computed using a rolling 10-minute smoothing window; sustained excess beyond the band averaged over that window counts toward overage. Short spikes (<=2 minutes) are ignored.

4) Fallback credit: if we fallback to an explicitly lower-capacity model (e.g., Redwood-7B variant) due to capacity constraints, we will issue a pro-rata service credit proportional to the time and requests affected, capped at 10% of the monthly reserved fee. Full details go in SOW / SLA section.

RPS to tokens/sec mapping: we estimate tokens/sec = sum_over_routes(RPS_route * avg_tokens_per_request_route). For sizing, we recommend customers provide a small telemetry sample (one hour) mapping RPS to average tokens/request per route. We can also run a quick profiling job on your traffic sample to propose the committed band.

Proposed commercial concession: for a 12-month commit at the 250k tokens/sec band we can do a 20% reserved-capacity discount and include one free capacity reconfiguration during the first 90 days. If you prefer a 24-month commit we can push the discount to 25%.

Attached: benchmark_results_v1.csv (sample mix), updated_pricing_model tab in the original spreadsheet.

Let me know if you want these terms in a short SOW for signature. Happy to set a lunchtime call to review the measurement runner.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: benchmark_results_v1.csv (CSV)]

Quick internal — Acme likes the math but asked for a stronger mid/long token mix; I've proposed shifting weights and offered 20% discount for 12-month at the 250k tokens/sec band (25% for 24-month). They also asked about fallback credits (pro-rata cap 10%).

Requesting approval to: 
- Lock discount at 20% for 12-month commit (approve commercial concession)
- Allow one free reconfiguration in first 90 days
- Accept fallback credit cap at 10% monthly fee (legal review pending)

Deal: ACME-DEAL-2027-09 — if approved I will prepare SOW + revised pricing sheet for signature.

Thanks,
Camila

I'll loop in Legal and Finance to fast-track the SOW and billing band language. Proceed to draft the SOW and ask Acme for the telemetry sample needed to convert RPS to tokens/sec.
